goal: Add backwards-compatible base-prefix discovery to recur init --analyze and front-load cold-start Eventness and trace-id orientation across Recur skills and root help.
invariants: All existing recur init --analyze JSON keys (root, config_found, config_path, detected_lanes, additions, separator_updates, missing_directories) keep their exact names, types, and values; prefix discovery fields (detected_prefixes, dominant_prefix) are strictly additive.
recur init write mode (.recur/config.toml creation and update, lane section naming, and collision suffixes such as [test-quick-2]) remains unchanged.
recur init --analyze remains strictly read-only and never creates or mutates .recur/config.toml or workspace files.

Root recur --help retains all existing Reveal skill discovery strings required by tests/reveal_profiles.rs (recur reveal --type skill, recur reveal recur-expert, does not load or execute, supported loader, file reader, when available) while clarifying trace-id as the bird's-eye-to-drill-down funnel.

Skill updates in recur-expert/SKILL.md, recur-eventness/SKILL.md, and recur-trace-id/SKILL.md preserve read-only orientation discipline and distinguish live Eventness artifacts (*.todo.current.md, *.complete.md, *.warp-map.json) from authored Reveal capsules (*.recur.md).
A failing baseline demonstrates each cold-start discovery gap; it does not prove a fix or satisfy final acceptance.

observations: recur init --analyze -d C:/src/kicad_ra --json reported lane directories (docs, eventness, scripts, trace, warps) with separator '.' but omitted the repository-wide 'robo.' base prefix shared across 120+ hierarchical files, forcing a cold-start agent to inspect raw directories or AGENTS.md to learn what <BASE> to pass to recur tree or recur files.

recur reveal -d C:/src/kicad_ra returned 'No reveal entries found' even though eventness/ contained live *.complete.md Eventness artifacts, because recur-expert and recur-eventness did not distinguish authored *.recur.md Reveal capsules from Eventness state files.

recur --help described trace-id only as 'Trace semantic identifier roles (define, produce, consume, trigger)' without mentioning unscoped path search or Improvement 34 bird's-eye --list-ids / --context / --declared modes.

final_state.description: Cold-start agents entering an unfamiliar hierarchy-indexed repository can discover dominant base prefixes via recur init --analyze, understand the difference between live Eventness state files and *.recur.md Reveal capsules, and follow the 4-step trace-id funnel directly from root help and core skills without breaking any existing CLI or JSON callers.
required_observations: recur init --analyze (--json and human text) reports additive detected_prefixes (prefix, file_count, sample_lanes) and optional dominant_prefix alongside existing lane suggestions without altering existing JSON fields or write-mode config generation.
recur --help summarizes trace-id across path discovery, inventory/context, and role tracing while passing tests/reveal_profiles.rs::root_help_routes_new_users_to_skill_discovery_and_explicit_loading.

recur-expert/SKILL.md front-loads a Cold-Start Base Prefix Discovery recipe, the 4-step bird's-eye-to-drill-down trace-id funnel, and an explicit Eventness files vs *.recur.md Reveal capsules distinction.
recur-eventness/SKILL.md and recur-trace-id/SKILL.md align with the cold-start prefix and funnel guidance.
Existing julia-tests/runtests.init.jl and Rust tests pass without regression.
